newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries paralysed in London amid data nerves.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries paralysed in London amid data nerves.

text.p: U.S Treasuries idled in slack trade in London on Friday as a dearth of fundamental news left dealers scabbling for direction. With several major reports due in the week ahead, investors were shying away.
"It's another exceptionally quiet morning, there's very lttle data due (on Friday) and everyone's just sitting back," said one dealer at a U.S. bank here.
"There's been a lot of issuance in the U.S. recently which has pushed things down, but everyone is waiting for the employment cost index on Tuesday."

By 0954 GMT, the 30-year long bond was at 93-22, to yield 7.14 percent, down from 93-23 in Tokyo and 93-25 at the New York close. Two-year paper was at an unchanged 99-23 and five-years was down a touch at 99-04 from 99-05 in Tokyo and New York.

Yamaichi International bond strategist Adam Chester said Treasuries would struggle to make much headway near term as a barrage of data next week will likely confirm the need for a further U.S. interest rate hike.
"Technically things aren't looking good," he said. "And the market is nervous about what will happen next week with the ECI on Tuesday, Q1 GDP data on Wednesday, culminating in payrolls on Friday."

He said all the data was expectecd to confirm the strength of the U.S. economy in Q1 and the need for a further Fed tightening. "So there's very little on the horizon which will be particularly supportive."

Chester said he expected a 25 basis point U.S. rate hike at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20, followed by another quarter point rise at the July 2 meeting. "Then we'll be back up to six percent and I think they'll leave it at that."

Existing homes sales data were due at 1400 GMT on Friday, expected to come in at 4.14 million in March. Chester said 106-14 was the next downside target for June T-bonds. "If we get strong data next week we'll test that and potentially go through it," he said, adding the long bond yield would likely target 7.25 percent.
By 1010 GMT, the June T-bond was down 4/32 in automated trade at 107-06.
